candidates.title: Audit app store discoverability signals

demandEvidence.chore: Finding ways for people to discover the author’s apps.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Built ASO Studio a couple of months ago because I had no idea how to get people to find my own apps.

experimentPlan.output: A reviewed checklist of public app listing fields and discoverability gaps.
experimentPlan.trigger: An app maker supplies one listing and a small set of target phrases.
steps: Compare it with supplied target phrases
Return a checklist for manual review
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Check that every checklist item points to text present in the supplied listing or phrase list.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: The maker supplies public material and decides whether to change a listing; no ranking or download outcome is promised.
unverified: The author’s tool capabilities and actual task details

ease.reason: A manual public-text review is possible, but no implementation evidence accompanies this post.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: independent app makers might pay for discoverability reviews; this post establishes no buyer intent.

feasibility.reason: A text-only checklist fits four weeks, but useful keyword comparison and ranking access are unverified.

autonomy.reason: The proposal drafts observations only; a person supplies data and makes every listing change.

evidence.reason: The post states a discoverability problem and that a tool was built, but supplies no workflow detail or corroboration.

candidates.reason: Fresh post describes difficulty getting apps found; a narrow listing review is testable but its buyer and utility remain unverified.

candidates.title: Draft an app review follow-up

demandEvidence.chore: Preparing a follow-up asking for an estimated review timeline or missing requirements.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Could you please share an estimated timeline, or let us know if anything is needed from our side?

experimentPlan.output: A concise follow-up message draft based on an operator-provided app submission timeline.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator enters the elapsed wait and current status.
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Confirm the draft contains no unsupported status or date and includes the requested question.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person checks facts and sends the message; the tool cannot review or expedite an app.
unverified: No source documents app-review APIs or status monitoring
Whether a follow-up is useful or receives a response

ease.reason: A small text drafting mock is approachable from operator-supplied facts; no implementation source is attached.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: app makers might pay for application follow-up help; this single request proves no market.

feasibility.reason: A four-week draft-only experiment is bounded, but platform-specific requirements and usefulness are unknown.

autonomy.reason: The draft is repeatable; a person supplies status, verifies it, and sends it.

evidence.reason: The retained span identifies a 55-day pending review and asks for timeline or missing needs; recurrence is unknown.

candidates.reason: The fresh retained post states a specific follow-up task, but the one case and unverified usefulness keep the draft below threshold.

candidates.title: Summarize public app security signals

demandEvidence.chore: Finding public information that helps an operator decide what to verify before installing a Shopify app.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: How can we know if a Shopify app is secure and trustworthy?

experimentPlan.output: A source-linked checklist of public security-related claims to verify manually.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator supplies an app listing for a pre-install review.
steps: Flag questions with no cited source
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Every checklist item must link to supplied public text; unresolved questions remain marked unknown.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person evaluates evidence and decides whether to install; the tool cannot certify security.
unverified: No authoritative Shopify security badge criteria supplied
Public statements may not prove security
No app listing or test evidence attached

ease.reason: A source-linked checklist is a modest manual prototype; no implementation reference is attached.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: store operators may pay for pre-install review; the question establishes no buying intent.

feasibility.reason: A four-week public-text prototype is bounded, but reliable criteria are unavailable.

autonomy.reason: The tool can organize supplied links, while a human judges risk and makes the decision.

evidence.reason: The post asks how to verify an app and mentions possible official marks; no criteria or corroboration are supplied.

candidates.reason: The question supports a narrow evidence-organizing mock, not a security verdict; criteria are missing and no buyer is established.

candidates.title: Flag duplicate workflow leads

demandEvidence.chore: Preventing repeated processing when a scheduled workflow trigger is missed.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: Missed schedule triggers can duplicate everything.

experimentPlan.output: A review table that flags likely duplicate lead records in a supplied sample.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator supplies two small sample batches for comparison.
steps: Flag possible repeats with matched fields
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Check labeled synthetic duplicate and distinct pairs against the flagged results.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person chooses match fields, confirms duplicates, and corrects or reruns the live workflow.
unverified: The span does not specify lead fields or matching rules
No source documents schedule recovery or idempotency support
No evidence that duplicate lead processing is this poster’s exact issue

ease.reason: A table-based mock can be attempted, but no attached reference documents record comparison.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: workflow consultants may pay to reduce duplicate processing; this maker post gives no customer evidence.

feasibility.reason: Synthetic pairs fit four weeks, but reliable keys and safe handling of live records remain unresolved.

autonomy.reason: The mock flags only; a human confirms matches and handles workflow recovery.

evidence.reason: The supplied span states missed schedule triggers can duplicate everything, but not a customer task, inputs, or frequency.

candidates.reason: A concrete operational risk is mentioned, but the supplied retained spans do not connect it to a specific paying customer task; provisional scope is a low-confidence mock.

candidates.title: Queue product image crop corrections

demandEvidence.chore: Repeatedly correcting product images that appear as square crops in a messaging app.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: I wish the image added for a product on the messaging app would default to the full size image and not a cut off square one, have to go in and correct it all the time.

experimentPlan.output: A manually reviewed queue of product images needing a full-size version.
experimentPlan.trigger: An operator adds an image that needs correction.
steps: Return the item for human image replacement
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Check that each synthetic item retains its product identifier and expected correction flag.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A person supplies images, confirms the desired version, and edits the messaging app; no image transformation is proposed.
unverified: No supplied source documents image rendition or messaging app integration
No evidence identifies the app or exact correction process

ease.reason: A manual queue is simple to mock, but no source supports image processing or messaging integration.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: merchants might pay to reduce recurring image corrections; the complaint establishes no payment intent.

feasibility.reason: A supplied-image checklist fits four weeks; actual full-size image handling is outside this scope.

autonomy.reason: A repeatable queue organizes work, but people supply and correct each image.

evidence.reason: The retained post says the person repeatedly corrects product images in a messaging app; specifics and corroboration are limited.

candidates.reason: The post explicitly describes repeated manual correction, but this proposal only organizes a queue and leaves image handling to a person; mean below six.

candidates.title: Review agent recovery scenarios

demandEvidence.chore: Designing checkpoint and recovery logic and handling repeated operations safely in agent systems.
demandEvidence.evidenceQuote: But devs need to write checkpointers, recovery logic, and deal with idempotency by theirselves.

experimentPlan.output: A scenario review worksheet listing recovery decisions and human-confirmed retry risks.
experimentPlan.trigger: A developer supplies one short synthetic task flow.
steps: List what state must be saved
experimentPlan.acceptanceCheck: Compare worksheet flags against a small set of operator-labeled synthetic failure cases.
experimentPlan.humanBoundary: A developer validates logic and authorizes any retry; worksheet does not execute recovery.
unverified: No implementation reference documents checkpoint persistence or idempotency
No concrete system or failure case appears in retained quote
No evidence of buyer intent or recurrence

ease.reason: This requires technical design judgment and no relevant implementation reference is supplied.

profit.reason: Hypothesis: agent developers might pay for recovery review; the post establishes no buyer demand.

feasibility.reason: A worksheet can be scoped, but usefulness depends on unspecified task architectures.

autonomy.reason: It organizes scenarios only; a developer must design, implement, and authorize recovery.

evidence.reason: The excerpt names three developer burdens but provides no specific incident, context or corroboration.

candidates.reason: A chore is stated generally, but no individual task context is given and the key recovery behavior is unsupported; no publication proposal.

rejected.title: WhatsApp connection authorization failure
rejected.reason: One specific integration bug report: the retained post describes a connection flow stuck before Meta authorization. A troubleshooting service would require platform diagnosis and access not supplied here; no repeatable bounded customer workflow is evidenced.

rejected.title: Document whether campaign pages should exist
rejected.reason: The retained post gives a personal heuristic about deleting pages without a purpose, then contains unrelated promotional text. It does not establish a requested service or sufficiently concrete customer chore.

rejected.title: Request feedback on an interview platform
rejected.reason: The only supplied text asks for product-functionality feedback. No specific usability problem, output, or task can be scoped without inventing one.

rejected.title: Understand copyright risks in LLM output
rejected.reason: The retained statement expresses a broad concern about rights in LLM output, but provides no concrete task, workflow, or requested service to adapt.
